title: Resumption Of Game Reviews And Another New Economy Index - Chinese Internet Weekly - Invesco China Technology ETF (NYSE:CQQQ)
text:
by ALT Perspective
Editors' Note: The Chinese Internet Weekly is published exclusively to SA Essential and PRO+ readers, and written by SA author ALT Perspective . It is published each Monday.
Market Briefs - Conflicting messages from trade talk outcome This week has been a busy one for the global stock market and the stocks in the Chinese Internet space are no exception. The week began riding on news of US President Trump and Chinese President Xi agreeing to a 90-day period for further discussions on trade before either side imposes additional tariffs on the other. The truce provided China with a breather from the originally anticipated increase in tariffs from 10 percent to 25 percent on $200 billion worth of goods on January 1, 2019.
Previously, President Trump had also threatened to impose tariffs on the remainder of Chinese imports, amounting to $267 billion based on 2017 data, which had yet to be slapped with tariffs. If he had gone ahead with the threat, Apple ( AAPL ) products manufactured in China would have been subjected to the new tariffs. There has been no further mention of this drastic measure for a while, allowing Apple investors to heave a sigh of relief.
While the trade war has, on the surface, nothing much to do with Chinese internet companies, it is well recognized from the comments in related threads on Seeking Alpha that the bearish sentiment brought about by the topic has clouded market confidence on all Chinese names.
KWEB Price data by YCharts KWEB Price data by YCharts
Across the board (referencing the top ten holdings of the KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF ( KWEB )( CWEB )( CQQQ )), there was a clear jump in stock prices when the market opened on Monday (December 3). Unfortunately, gains fizzled out by the end of Tuesday as the highly positive take on the outcome of the trade talks over the weekend at Argentina by President Trump did not correspond with the same from the Chinese side. The return of harsh rhetoric by the self-proclaimed 'Tariff Man' sank the stock markets further on Tuesday.
Chinese internet stocks fared better for the week After the midweek trading break for a day of mourning the death of former President George H.W. Bush on Wednesday, the stock markets resumed markedly lower. Although there was a rebound by the end of the day, mixed signals from the White House led to market confusion again on Friday. At the same time that White House economic adviser Larry Kudlow expressed optimism over the trade talks on CNBC, trade adviser Peter Navarro was threatening on CNN the imposition of higher tariffs if there is no resolution regarding the trade impasse following the 90-day negotiating period.
Nevertheless, the Chinese internet sector managed to hang onto their superior performance for the week, thanks to a better head start, as well as a bullish policy development benefiting NetEase ( NTES ) and Tencent ( OTCPK:TCEHY )( OTCPK:TCTZF ). There were also interesting partnership activities happening at Tencent and JD.com ( JD ) which probably supported sentiment towards the two companies. The three stocks represented around a quarter of KWEB by weight, based on the data as of September 30, 2018, the last update available from the ETF.
KWEB Price data by YCharts
Momo Inc was the outlier due to downside guidance Video streaming and dating services provider, Momo Inc ( MOMO ), was the outlier for the week. Momo represented 5 percent of the weight of KWEB. By midday on Friday, it lost nearly a third of its value as compared to the start of the week. The trigger for the 14.6 percent loss on Thursday was the downside guidance issued alongside the Q3 2018 results release . Momo dropped another 9.2 percent ostensibly after a downgrade from Morgan Stanley ( MS ) from Overweight to Equal Weight. The investment bank also more than halved its price target on Momo from $61 to $30.
Momo's 3Q 2018 results were actually a beat both on the revenue and the EPS on a non-GAAP basis. It achieved a revenue of $535.97 million, up 51.2 percent over the same quarter in the previous year and higher than the consensus estimate by $1.97 million. Its non-GAAP EPS of $0.53 was higher than the consensus estimate by $0.07 but on a GAAP basis, the EPS of $0.39 missed by $0.03.
The accompanying press release listed five reasons for the 66 percent year-on-year increase in cost and expenses (see below quotation). Key among these, I believe, is related to the continuous fight for quality broadcasters amid keener competition for users and advertising dollars, factors which I had elaborated in my initiation article on YY Inc ( YY ), its main rival in the video streaming space.
Cost and expenses were $442.1 million in the third quarter of 2018, an increase of 66% from $266.3 million in the third quarter of 2017. The increase was primarily attributable to: a) an increase in revenue sharing with the broadcasters related to our live video service and virtual gift recipients; b) the produced contents in connection with Phanta City; c) an increase in personnel related costs including share-based compensation expenses as a result of the Company's rapidly expanding talent pool; d) an increase in marketing and promotional expenses to enhance our brand awareness and attract users; and e) an increase in amortization expenses related to the intangible assets from acquisitions.
As a result of Momo's downside guidance and subsequent share price plunge, its industry peers, Huya Broadcasting ( HUYA ), and YY Inc also suffered collateral damages. The latter two dropped 14.1 percent and 4.5 percent respectively over the past five-day trading period, compared with 18.9 percent for Momo.
MOMO Price data by YCharts
Note that Momo's share price peaked in June this year but the stock suffered from a short-seller attack soon after. I wrote a rebuttal to some of the points stated in the short-seller report. Ben Axler, the point man behind Spruce Point Capital, the issuer of the report, took a cheap shot in the comments field in my article but did not refute any of my rebuttals. Although Momo is now trading near its 52-week low, much of the weakness is attributable to several factors not targeted by the short-seller claims. Nevertheless, the factors mentioned by J Capital in its short pitch for Momo at the recent Kase Learning Short-Selling Conference sounded more credible. These included lower MAUs growth potential, high political risk, and 'massive insider selling'.
End of China's freeze on new video games? Shares of NetEase roared on Thursday upon receiving an upgrade from Morgan Stanley . The investment bank raised its price target on the American depositary receipts ('ADRs') of NetEase to $300 from $260 and changed its recommendation to Overweight from Equal Weight. The price target represented a 31 percent upside based on Tuesday's closing price. The consensus price target is some $43 higher than the current price.
NTES data by YCharts
Nevertheless, looking at the tepid share price movement of Tencent, perhaps the bigger news regarding the possible thawing of the new video games approval freeze in China have yet to be fully absorbed by the market. Reports emerged on Friday that an assessment committee has been set up to ensure only online games that meet a certain code of ethics are approved for release to the public. The Publicity Department of the Communist Party of China ('CPC') Central Committee said on Friday the move is to provide the public with 'healthy entertainment products' and 'protect adolescents' from the negative impact of online gaming.
While the assessment committee has outright rejected nine games submitted for approval, 11 games remained in the running if the relevant online gaming producers and operators could make 'adjustments' to the 'controversial contents' in them. It was not mentioned which of the games belonged to Tencent or NetEase but the two are among the biggest game producers and operators in China and are likely to benefit from the resumption of game approvals. Wall Street Journal quoted a researcher in estimating that the game approval freeze has resulted in game companies losing around $200 million in revenue a month.
New Economy Index hits a new high for 2018 In the previous edition, I wrote about a new index released by the National Bureau of Statistics (‘NBS’) of China seeking to track the progress of China’s economic transformation and upgrading , such as the shift to online retailing and high-tech manufacturing. Roughly translated as the ‘new growth drivers’ index, the numbers for 2015 to 2017 at 123.5, 156.7, and 210.1, respectively, reflect a yoy increase of 23.5 percent, 26.9 percent, and 34.1 percent. This is a clear acceleration, albeit based on a short three-year data. The NBS defined the new economy as industries engaging in activities leading to new scientific and technological outcomes as well as new forms of commercial activities derived from traditional sectors and new business models.
This week, I introduce another gauge that is also aimed at tracking the 'new economy' - the Mastercard Caixin BBD New Economy Index ('NEI'). Based on the definition of the NEI, a 'new economy' industry is one that is labor-and technology-intensive but asset-light; at the same time, it experiences sustainable and rapid growth.
On Monday, the November NEI was made available, showing a climb from October’s 29.8 to 31.33, the highest reading since December 2017. This implied that the 'new economy' industries represented 31.33 percent of China’s overall economic input, marking its rising importance in the broader economy. According to Caixin Insight Group, the NEI measures labor, capital, and technology inputs in 10 emerging industries relative to those in all industries.
Among the 10 tracked industries, the new information and technology sector (abbreviated as 'New IT' in the following chart) held onto its pole position as the top contributor and also expanded its share of the NEI reading by 1.3 percentage points from October to 12.1 percentage points. This bodes well for the Chinese internet stocks.
A less precise but nonetheless relevant index, the Caixin China General Services PMI, also has a positive message for the technology sector. The seasonally adjusted Caixin China General Services Business Activity Index jumped from October’s 13-month low of 50.8 to 53.8 in November . In particular, services companies expressed the steepest increase in total new orders since June during November. This comes even as the PMI for the manufacturing activities was little-changed from October’s reading of 50.1 at 50.2 in November, reflecting the dual-tracked economy.
Market Outlook A speculative report that surfaced late in the week could influence the stock price movement of Tencent next week. The Information reported that Alphabet's unit, Google ( GOOG )( GOOGL ), had been 'secretly exploring ways' to partner with Tencent to offer Google Cloud services in the mainland . If the plan comes to fruition, corporate customers using Google Cloud’s software tools and services outside of the mainland could rely on similar tools and services from Tencent when on the mainland. Such a speculation is not new, as Bloomberg had reported on Google's intentions in early August , for which I wrote about as well. Nevertheless, it seems the progress is more concrete this time around.
For JD.com, Nikkei Asian Review reported on Friday another development in the company's online-to-offline push . JD.com has opened a hydroponic vegetable factory in Beijing, in partnership with Mitsubishi Chemical ( OTCPK:MTLHY )( OTCPK:MTLHF ). JD.com will begin online sales shortly of the lettuce and about five other leafy vegetables grown at the factory. Xiaosong Wang, the head of the company's food businesses, said that JD.com will leverage its e-commerce and logistics expertise to bring safe and fresh foods to consumer tables.
On the macro side, the General Administration of Customs ('GAC') of China is scheduled to release the November trade data on December 8. The numbers could appease the Trump administration somewhat if the imports from the US rose. On the other hand, unfavorable numbers could provide more fodder for President Trump to attack China and the consequent negative impact on the stock markets.
Later in the week, on Tuesday, the November number for vehicle sales is due. On Friday, we will have the industrial production and retail sales data for November. Last month's retail figures are worthy to watch as that's when the Singles' Day online shopping extravaganza occurred.
What's your take? Are you getting more confident of the prospects facing the Chinese internet stocks? Is there something significant that happened or on the horizon that I have missed out? Please freely share your insights, thoughts, and let me know if you found this article useful or provide your feedback in the comments section.
Disclosure: I am/we are long BABA, TCEHY, JD, NTES.
